What do these terms mean?
NDVI
A greenness score from satellite images. Higher means denser plants. Built-up land and water score low.
Water share
The percentage of a zone covered by water.
Risk
The chance a zone drops below your green or water limit in the next 12 months. Shown as low, medium or high.
Critical NDVI (τ)
The greenness level below which a zone counts as at risk.
Benefit score
A unitless score for how much a spending plan helps. Compare plans with each other, not with outside numbers.
Forecast range
The shaded band on charts. A wide band means low certainty.

Budget plan

How the money is best shared across zones.

Expected benefit by strategy

Same budget, different strategies. Benefit is a unitless score (higher is better). "No action" scores zero by definition.

Benefit vs budget

Returns diminish as budget grows. The dot marks the current budget.

Priority ranking and recommended allocation (top 10 zones)

Allocation maximises Σ V·(0.15+R)·(1−e^(−k·x)) subject to Σ cost·x ≤ budget and 0 ≤ x ≤ 30 lakh per zone. Money goes where the benefit per rupee is equal across funded zones (shadow price λ = ). R is combined risk, 1 − (1 − Rgreen)(1 − Rwater). V is conservation value (1 to 10, set by the team). Cost factor and response rate k are assumed values.
6

How this was made

Data, cleaning and limits.

Data and method

Pipeline
  • Imagery: COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED, 10 m, cloud and shadow pixels removed with the SCL band.
  • Composites: monthly median, 36 months (2023-01 to 2025-12).
  • Green cover: NDVI = (B8 − B4) / (B8 + B4); mean per zone.
  • Water: MNDWI = (B3 − B11) / (B3 + B11); water if > 0; reported as % of zone area.
  • Forecast: linear trend plus monthly seasonality, 12 months ahead, with a 90% range.
  • Satellite images: annual median Sentinel-2 composites made by export_kumaraswamy.py: true colour (B4,B3,B2), false colour (B8,B4,B3), NDVI map and water mask.
Data cleaning and assumptions
  • NDVI and water % per zone and month come from zone_timeseries.csv (20 zones × 36 months).
  • 96 zone-months were empty (monsoon cloud) and 22 were removed as outliers (cloud or shadow contamination). All were filled by linear interpolation between neighbouring months.
  • A zone counts as a water zone if its typical water share is at least 2.4%. Urban shadows add about 1% everywhere, so small values are not lakes.
  • Conservation value V, cost factors and response rates are team assumptions, not measured.
Known limits
  • Surface water only; groundwater is not measured.
  • Zones with a lot of water (for example Zone 15) show low NDVI because water reflects almost no near-infrared light, so their green-cover risk is overstated. Treat their NDVI risk with care.
  • Three years is short, so forecasts are indicative.
  • Monsoon cloud leaves gaps; consider Sentinel-1 radar for water.
Imagery: Copernicus Sentinel-2, processed with Google Earth Engine. Advisory only: forecasts are indicative and should be checked by a local expert before any action.
